full_judgment: 5. Mr. Asrarul Hossain referred to a notification dated 20.10.84 by which the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka has been given teritorial jurisdiction over the whole District of Dhaka (i.e. District Court of Dhaka) in respect of suits relating to Bank loans and other Banking matters. In other words, by this notification the Court of the District Judge of Dhaka and the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 had been put at par with regard to the territorial jurisdiction of the District of Dhaka (i.e. the District Court of Dhaka). Further, the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka has been given exclusive jurisdiction to try all suits in respect of the matters covered by the above notification. In view of the above notification, he submits that the jurisdiction of the Court of the District Judge has been ousted in respect of the suits covered by the above notification. The Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka has exclusive jurisdiction to take cognizance of the suits covered by the above notification and no other Court including the Court of the District Judge has the jurisdiction to take cognizance of such suits. Mr. Asrarul Hossain also submits that in respect of the suits covered by the above notification the limitation as to pecuniary jurisdiction of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 under section 19 of the Act will not be applicable inasmuch as the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 can take cognizance of a suit of any value for recovery of Bank loan. In other words, the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in respect of suits covered by the above notification is not controlled by section 19 of the Act. Both the Courts, the court of District Judge and the Court of the Subordinate Judge, have unlimited concurrent pecuniary jurisdiction to try all original suits cognizable by Civil Courts of which the value exceeds Taka 50,000/-(Section 18 read with section 19 of the Act) Mr. Asrarul Hossain further submits that the decree in question has been passed in respect of a loan advanced by the decree holders petitioner, Sonali Bank, as such the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka had exclusive jurisdiction to entertain the certified copy of the decree in question under Section 44A(1) of the Code. He also referred to section 15 of the Code in support of his contention that the certified copy of the decree in question under section 44A(1) of the Code had rightly been filed in the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka. Under section 15 of the Code every suit shall be instituted in the Court of the lowest grade competent to try it and the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka is the Court of the lowest grade competent to try such suit out of which the present decree had been passed.
